title: langgraph.errors.InvalidUpdateError: Must write to at least one of ['foo']
observed_behavior: Two class-based nodes return dicts typed as a second schema (TmpState with 'zoo'), while the graph's state schema declares only 'foo'. node_1 completes, then the graph raises InvalidUpdateError: Must write to at least one of ['foo']. The user expected {'foo': 3}.
structure_focus: Node return keys outside the graph's declared state schema; class-based nodes with foreign return annotations
notes: Closed, no labels. The maintainer could not reproduce the reported error on the original snippet and the reporter's own environment/version remained inconsistent, so the observed behavior is not fully confirmed; on the repository's pinned langgraph 1.0.3 this fixture also completes with {'foo': 3} rather than raising. Structurally, a node may only update keys declared on the graph's state schema; returning only 'zoo' cannot update 'foo', which is the composition lesson. This is a usage/schema misunderstanding rather than a framework defect; the non-reproduction is preserved because it limits how strongly the fixture can be said to reproduce anything.
